claims.claim: Reviewers report technical issues with the PC port, including stuttering, constant frame drops, and resolution limitations.

citations.review_text: Very Poor PC Performance. I can handle a 60fps locked game, but this one stutters constantly and drops to 20-30 fps every minute.

In good conciousness I cannot recommend this port of DS3, it is laggy and full of bugs that prevent the game from running. I have played 100's of hours of DS3 on PS4-5. This bums me out incredibly with how badly it runs. Not only can you not full screen it, unless its in windowed mode with another application. It simply cannot run on a higher resolution then 1080p. Its a great game, but this port is not worth the consistant $60 asking price on steam.

claims.claim: Mouse and keyboard controls receive criticism for lacking proper layouts, menus, and instructions, effectively requiring a controller to play comfortably.

citations.review_text:
Mouse and keyboard controls are absolutely terrible. The game looks great and I get the hype, but this is the lowest-effort PC port I have ever seen. I have never seen a developer so full of themselves that they think players can be expected to buy a controller and learn how to play with it, simply because they were too lazy to implement a decent layout for a platform where the majority of people use a mouse and keyboard.

TL;DR: The game never gives you a proper button layout, providing zero help in the menus or during gameplay. You literally have to look up shortcuts on the internet just to play. If you don't have a controller, be prepared to be deeply disappointed.
idk why this game is so popular tbh - most of the time you're fighting the clunky camera, the super low FOV, and the clunky controls

citations.review_text: Very high learning curve and a very difficult game, but worth it. Insane game.

cohorts.label: 20-100h
cohorts.summary: Experienced players note that side quests remain cryptic without outside walkthroughs.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that NPC questlines are cryptic and easily missed without following an online guide.

citations.review_text:
**Recommended 👍**

Dark Souls III had me hooked from the start. The combat is fun, the bosses are awesome, and it has that classic Souls challenge that keeps you saying, "One more try."

There are some quality-of-life improvements over the previous game, which make the experience feel a bit smoother overall.

I still think the first Dark Souls is the better game, but this one is fantastic in its own right.

My only real complaints are that it felt a bit too long, and the NPC questlines are way too cryptic. Unless you're following a guide, it's ridiculously easy to miss them. I think I only completed one questline and accidentally skipped all the others. 😂

Overall, I had a great time and would definitely recommend it. Just be prepared to die... a lot.

Dark Souls 3 is my least favourite out of all the Soulsborne but as a game alone it stands out to other games I have played, it features some of the best bosses of all time, great areas with the most stunning landscape I have ever seen, and touching npc's questline, (although the overall quest design sucked), but it doesn't matter that much since the game balances it out with very good voice acting anyways. it also features real fun weapon to use with some really cool flashy moveset and they deal great damages too (if you build your character right)

But of course there is some downside to it aswell like Farron Keep, progress feels too linear limiting in some freedom of your build, and the server sucks so bad (this keeps happening to me and my friend whenever we try to do co-op together, seriously whats with japanese and their bad server but great game?) Strength build felt weak in this game, and lastly why did they remove the ability to level up at the bonfire, it's really annoying having to warp to Firelink Shrine each time you want to level your stats up.

However some of the bosses in this game are just pure gem, a carefully crafted piece of art, greatly design bossfight, and most of them has become my favourites bossfights among all of the Soulsborne, so if you desire fun and challenging bossfight with epic orchestra echoing your ears, then this game is definitely for you.

Lastly, i will recommend this game to everyone who's new to the Soulsborne series, or someone who's into Soulsborne but hasn't played this game yet.

7.8/10.

cohorts.label: 100h+

claims.claim: Reviewers characterize the map design as more linear and less interconnected compared to the first installment in the series.

citations.review_text:
The definitive Dark Souls experience MINUS the amazingly interconnected map of DS1. 

It's gorgeous, it's smooth, stellar voice acting, none of the jank of the older titles (love them anyway).

Perfect game. All time goat.

10 years later. Post 100%-ing the game. One of the best to ever do it. Can be a touch linear compared to the original installment, but it makes up for it in style, atmosphere, and satisfaction. A number one spot contender if there ever was one.

While I still have a soft spot for the first game and prefer PvP in Dark Souls 2 but Dark Souls 3 is an excellent conclusion to the trilogy and a fantastic action RPG in its own right. The game leans heavily into fan service, bringing back familiar characters, locations and references to Dark Souls 1. Sometimes it feels a little too nostalgic.

Many encounters are challenging, visually spectacular and require learning enemy patterns rather than simply relying on high level equipment. The fights I remember the most are against the Nameless King, the Dancer of the Boreal Valley and the final boss. Each of them feels unique, demanding and incredibly satisfying to overcome.

The world design may not be as interconnected as the original Dark Souls, but the locations are still memorable and beautifully crafted. Every area has its own atmosphere, secrets and enemies that make exploring enjoyable from beginning to end.

The PC version is also a solid way to experience the game, offering smooth performance and good controls, especially compared to console versions.

Pros:

+ Fantastic boss fights
+ Great atmosphere
+  Beautiful world and level design
+  Excellent soundtrack (Abyss Watchers <3)
+  Smooth and satisfying combat

Cons:

- Relies a bit too much on fan service
- For me world is less interconnected than Dark Souls I
- Fewer truly new ideas than previous entries

After completing Dark Souls 1 and 2, I had to play the 3, and what an amazing game it is, but weirdly it is the one I enjoyed the least. But it doesn't mean that it's a bad game. So even though I loved it, I still have a few things to say.

Whether it's how it was intended or maybe the fact that I now have years of Souls-like, I found it a bit easy, to the point where some of the bosses were a bit disappointing and I felt like I couldn't appreciate them to their full extent, and having beat the game and DLC in around 30-40 hours, it's not like I was overleveled.

I thought it was a bit more straightforward, more linear compared to his two little brothers. It's not a bad thing, but I really felt this lack of freedom.

Like Elden Ring is the most accessible FromSoftware game in general, DS3 is the most accessible Dark Souls game in my opinion. It looks nice, you always know what to do or where to go, there are no major roadblocks (from my experience), and the movements were already what we know from today's FromSoftware games and not the truckload of a character you had to carry in the previous games. And for the best or the worst, I feel that DS3 is missing this single zone that you hate with all your soul.

I'll never repeat this enough, but Dark Souls games are NOT HARD. You just need to forget all those speedrunners or min-maxing players and just try to see what fits your playstyle. Use the items and tools the game gives you and play at your own pace. If you struggle against a boss, it's all good, no one is asking you to one-try them. Go back, level up, strengthen your gear, and then go back to the boss. (Except if trying again and again is your go-to, which I'd understand, I'm like that too.)

Like always in Dark Souls games, you're free to do whatever you want with your build, daggers, swords, heavy weapons, bows, magic, incantations, focusing on one thing, or mixing everything is up to you and what you're comfortable with. All enemies and bosses have resistance…

claims.claim: Reviewers note the absence of native cloud save support in the game.

citations.review_text:
Spoiler-Free Review:
Finished replaying the base game for the second time just now, and went ahead and finished both the DLCs for the first time. Not realizing that there wasn't cloud saves for this one made me go through another playthrough to get to the DLCs but I'm not mad, rather happy that I got to play it through with another class and another playstyle. For the base game, you'll realise soon enough why it's considered to be a tough game. It's oppressive as hell, but if you push ahead, nothing will permanently stop you. You adapt, you learn and you ultimately get past areas, bosses, and yourself. The optional bosses in the base game are arguably the best that it has to offer, so don't miss out. As for the DLCs, Ashes of Ariandel was a mixed bag for me, with an okayish environment that got old fast, and enemies that were a bit tedious to get away from. As for the bosses, the main boss is a endurance fight, one of the very best in the game, and the length of it caught me off guard. As for the Ringed City DLC, I enjoyed it a lot. The traversal and the design of the map was top notch, and the enemies, while brutal, are satisfying to beat. The two main bosses not counting the semi npc fight, were astonishingly good, and epic. The optional boss is proabably the hardest boss in the game and one of the toughest, yet one of the coolest bosses to fight and defeat. The game brings the Dark Souls saga to a close in a beautiful manner, melancholic in a way, with the best feeling boss fight, and a sombre close to the chapter of the Dark Soul.
This game is not for everyone. It can be highly oppressive at times, and borderline confusing during phases, but it is cathartic in its satisfaction of a playthrough, and it's maybe why, people continue to flock into souls games. Good luck, Ashen One. 
9.5/10.
The game itself is really good but the developers still haven't enabled cloud saves. After losing a 550 hour save because I had to reinstall windows, I can't recommend it.

claims.claim: Reviewers highlight that the combat features a faster pace compared to previous titles in the series.

citations.review_text:
Well better late than never.

I finished this game for the first time over 5 years ago but life happened and now having replayed it I feel like leaving a review is the right thing to do. Especially since I'm a big FromSoftware fan and I want to finish as many of their games as possible.

Since the game is getting a bit old by now and newcomers might be coming from either Dark Souls Remastered or more likely Elden Ring I will try to make the review with a more broad view of the Dark Souls series and Elden Ring in view.


For anybody that has played Elden Ring and wants to play this entry in FromSoft's lineup then good news you will most likely adapt very quickly to the general speed of this game.
I do understand that going from a massive open world to a more level based experience can be jarring but in my opinion that can be adapted to easily enough. Just think of the game as Elden Ring's legacy dungeons tied together and cut out the rest.

For those coming from either the first or second game then the first major difference you will feel is the speed of the combat.

Everything feels like it's been sped up a bit and a lot of the enemies are either smarter than the previous 2 games or have more "surprising" attacks. Think of a normal low level enemy using a longer melee weapon that can hit a much larger area around said enemy and thus catch you even when you thought you were in a safe zone.

Level design is still solid. At least from my point of view there are no awful zones in this iteration of the series.
Even the 1 poison swamp isn't that particularly bad or drawn out.

Enemy variety is quite nice but Elden Ring players especially will recognize quite a few enemies that behave almost the same as their ER incarnations. This by itself shouldn't be necessarily a big minus since fans of their games more or less expect some reusing of assets but if you've only played ER then seeing a number of enemies be almost copies from their newer game might throw you off.

As is us…
Classic Dark Souls experience, with a faster pace than DS2. Incredibly gorgeous graphics and excellent world to explore.
